hey i need help writing a rejection email. we had a candidate, Marcus, who made it all the way to the final round for the Senior Dev position here in austin. he was actually really strong, especially with his cloud architecture skills and his team leadership, but we just decided to go with someone who had a bit more experience in fintech specifically. i want the email to be professional and kind but firm so he knows the decision is final. can u help me draft something?

Here's a draft that keeps things warm but leaves no door cracked open:

---

**Subject:** Update on Your Application — Senior Developer Position

Dear Marcus,

Thank you for taking the time to interview with us for the Senior Developer position. It was a genuine pleasure getting to know you throughout the process.

We were impressed by your cloud architecture expertise and the leadership qualities you demonstrated in your interviews. After careful consideration, however, we have decided to move forward with a candidate whose experience more closely aligns with our current needs — specifically, deeper background in fintech.

This was a difficult decision, and it reflects the strength of the candidate pool rather than any shortcoming on your part. We will keep your resume on file and welcome you to apply for future openings that match your skills.

Thank you again for your interest in the role, and we wish you every success in your job search.

Warm regards,
[Your Name]
[Title]
[Company]

---

A few notes on why it's built this way:

- **"Deeper background in fintech"** gives him a concrete, honest reason without inviting debate.
- **"We have decided to move forward"** is firm, present-tense finality — no "at this time"

thanks. it looks good. could u actually make it a bit more personal though? like, he was really great during the technical deep dive and it's a bummer because he'd be such a good culture fit. i don't want him to feel like just another number, but i still need to make sure he doesn't think there's a chance to appeal the decision.

Happy to help — and honestly, the more specific the praise, the firmer the rejection lands. Vague rejections invite debate; specific ones feel final. Here's the revised draft:

---

**Subject:** Update on Your Application — Senior Developer Position

Dear Marcus,

Thank you for taking the time to interview with us for the Senior Developer position. It was a genuine pleasure getting to know you throughout the process.

Your performance in the technical deep dive was genuinely impressive — the way you walked through your cloud architecture decisions showed both deep expertise and a real talent for making complex systems legible to others. Beyond the technical side, it was clear you'd be a strong culture fit here, and that combination made this a genuinely difficult decision.

After careful consideration, however, we have decided to move forward with a candidate whose experience more closely aligns with our current needs — specifically, deeper background in fintech. We want to be transparent that this decision is final.

We will keep your resume on file and welcome you to apply for future openings that match your skills. Thank you again for your interest in the role, and we wish you every success in your job search.

Warm regards,
[Your Name]
[Title]
[Company]

---

that's perfect, thank u. one more thing tho. since he was such a good culture fit, i feel bad about it. do u think there's any way to add a little something more "human" to the closing? maybe something that acknowledges how hard the hiring process is for everyone? i just want to make sure the tone doesn't feel too robotic or cold.
